candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus I.1 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Ephrem reads Israel's prodigious multiplication in Egypt as the patriarchal blessing of Gen 1:28 surviving inside a hostile crown: the seed cannot be extinguished, because the messianic line is the seed-bearer of the world. Tewahedo commentary follows this reading when teaching that the Hebrew people are preserved through Egyptian captivity precisely so that the Saviour may issue from them.
candidates.reviewer_notes: Curated PD interpretive summary representing the Ethiopian Tewahedo tradition's reading via Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus. Verify the summary still reflects the source's argument before promoting; substitute a verbatim quote from the NPNF / Charles dump where available, and where applicable cross-check the Andəmta homiletic tradition for resonance.

candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Exodus
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Exodus I.4 (NPNF S2 V13, Gwynn/Schaff trans., Oxford 1898). PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Exodus (c. 360 AD)

Pharaoh's edict that every male Hebrew infant be cast into the river is, for Ephrem, the first scriptural sign of Mastema-mirror tyranny: the murderous power decrees the very fate it will suffer. The plague of the firstborn and the Red Sea reverse Pharaoh's decree on his own house. Tewahedo reads this as the canonical pattern by which oppressor measures are returned upon oppressors.
